output.brief: The rejections were caused by the wrong refrigeration setpoint on Meridane containers. When the Tallis documentation suite went live for Meridane bookings, the mandarin product record was created by copying an avocado record, so it carries 7.0°C instead of the 4.0°C mandarin specification. The five rejected containers were all booked that way, and their controllers ran to 7°C as instructed. The two Meridane containers at 4°C (K1) passed, and the 4°C Coastway and Tallis-free containers passed too. The fungicide change, Lower Serra fruit and transit time do not explain the pattern. Meridane's "units worked to setpoint" reply is true but beside the point, so a refrigeration-failure claim would likely fail and would hide our own error. I am fairly confident (about 85%) in this, since the setpoint records match the decay pattern. Next: correct PRD-MAND-01 to 4.0°C now, and ask Meridane to reset the queued 10 Oct container and the one at sea before it arrives. Hold the Lower Serra suspension, the Meridane claim and the Brindle deduction until the record error is confirmed. Add a check that compares reefer settings with the product specification, and place independent loggers in containers for verification.
